sources_considered.why: Primary multi-model chess experiment distinguishes legal moves, completed games and playing strength.
Primary contemporary experiment with a documented prompt and linked game records provides counterevidence to blanket inability.

evidence_items.locator: gpt-4 (aka ChatGPT-4), Move ability against SF
evidence_items.explanation: Repeated illegal moves support the reliability criticism of GPT-4. The same results also contain many fully legal games, so they do not establish complete inability to play.

The experiment reports 11 wins in 19 GPT-3.5 games using the full move sequence each turn, with game links provided. It contradicts blanket inability across general-purpose systems, while its occasional illegal moves and small sample limit the reliability conclusion.

unresolved_gaps: No single threshold distinguishes handling a game from handling it unreliably.
The retained tests mainly concern chess and do not establish performance across all fixed-rule games.
The small successful-play experiment is not a comprehensive independent replication.
